title: Kingdom/Domain Placement
cheat_card: Three-Domain System: Organisms are classified into Domains Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya based on ribosomal RNA (rRNA) sequence differences.
Archaea vs. Bacteria: Archaea share a more recent common ancestor with Eukarya than with Bacteria, biochemically resembling Eukarya, and lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls.

Eukaryotic Supergroups: Kingdom Protista is polyphyletic (six distinct evolutionary lines) and classified into six Supergroups: Archaeplastida, Chromalveolata, Excavata, Amoebazoa, Opisthokonta, and Rhizaria.
Fungi and Animal Clade: Fungi and animals belong to the same supergroup, Opisthokonta, making them more closely related to each other than either is to plants (which belong to Archaeplastida).
Virus Exclusion: Viruses are excluded from the domains of life because they are non-cellular, lack metabolism, and cannot respond to stimuli.
memory_anchor:
### The Three Domains and Eukaryotic Supergroups

| Domain / Group | Cell Wall Material | Key rRNA & Evolutionary Status | Organism Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Domain Bacteria** | Peptidoglycan | Distinct bacterial rRNA; prokaryotic | E. coli, Cyanobacteria |
| **Domain Archaea** | No Peptidoglycan | Archaeal rRNA; biochemically closer to Eukarya | Halophiles, Methanogens |
| **Domain Eukarya** | Cellulose (Plants) or Chitin (Fungi) | Eukaryotic rRNA; divided into 6 Supergroups | Plants, Animals, Fungi, Protists |
| *Supergroup Archaeplastida* | Cellulose | Contains plastids from cyanobacteria | Land plants, Red & Green Algae |
| *Supergroup Opisthokonta* | Chitin (Fungi) or None (Animals) | Fungi and animals form a sister clade | Mushroom, Sponges, Humans |

flashcards.q: Why is the traditional Kingdom Protista no longer considered a valid clade, and what taxonomic group replaces it in modern classification?
flashcards.a: Protists are not monophyletic; DNA evidence shows they represent six distinct evolutionary lineages that did not evolve from a single common ancestor. In modern systematics, they are split into six Supergroups, which represent separate evolutionary lines that rank below Domain but above Kingdom.

flashcards.q: Describe two major biochemical or structural differences that distinguish Domain Archaea from Domain Bacteria, despite both being prokaryotic.
flashcards.a: First, Archaea lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls, which is a defining component of bacterial cell walls. Second, the base sequence of Archaea ribosomal RNA (rRNA) differs significantly from Bacteria, biochemically aligning them more closely with Eukarya.

flashcards.q: Which eukaryotic supergroups do land plants, fungi, and animals belong to, and what does this reveal about their evolutionary relationships?
flashcards.a: Land plants belong to the supergroup Archaeplastida. Fungi and animals both belong to the supergroup Opisthokonta. This classification shows that fungi and animals share a more recent common ancestor and are more closely related to each other than either is to land plants.

outline_blanks: The tree of life is organized into three domains based on rRNA differences, where Domain [[Archaea]] lacks peptidoglycan and is biochemically more similar to Domain [[Eukarya]] than to Domain [[Bacteria]]. In eukaryotic classification, organisms are grouped into six [[Supergroups]], meaning that plants belong to [[Archaeplastida]] while fungi and animals are closely related within [[Opisthokonta]]. In contrast, [[Viruses]] are not placed in any kingdom or domain because they are non-cellular and not considered living.
